When a VAT return is due

A period that ends on the last day of a month is due on the 7th of the month after next. A quarter that ends on 31 March is due on 7 May.

The deadline for submitting your return online is usually one calendar month and 7 days after the end of an accounting period.

gov.uk/vat-returns/deadlines Retrieved 13 November 2026

Penalty points and the threshold

Each late return adds one point until you reach the threshold of your accounting period.

Return Points threshold Compliance period Returns
Annually 2 24 months 2
Quarterly 4 12 months 4
Monthly 5 6 months 6
Source: the table on gov.uk/guidance/penalty-points-and-penalties-if-you-submit-your-vat-return-late Retrieved 13 November 2026

When you reach the threshold, you’ll receive a £200 penalty. You’ll also receive a further £200 penalty for each subsequent late submission while you’re at the threshold.

gov.uk/guidance/penalty-points-and-penalties-if-you-submit-your-vat-return-late Retrieved 13 November 2026

What removes points

Below the threshold, points expire on their own.

At the threshold, you remove the points when you meet both conditions: a period of compliance, and every outstanding return of the previous 24 months.

Source: the table on gov.uk/guidance/remove-penalty-points-youve-received-after-submitting-your-vat-return-late Retrieved 13 November 2026

A: complete a period of compliance, submitting all returns by the deadline. B: submit all outstanding returns for the previous 24 months.

gov.uk/guidance/remove-penalty-points-youve-received-after-submitting-your-vat-return-late Retrieved 13 November 2026
